verdicts: The world is a fair test: an informed entity that only walks in circles dies of the hidden need in at least 90% of worlds, an informed entity that learns the skill ladder almost never does, and it survives at least twice as well as chance
circles-only informed dies of hidden need in 100% of worlds; skill-ladder informed in 0%; deaths per 10k 0.0 vs chance 102.0
Listening to boredom fills the hidden need better than ignoring it (hidden-need level in the last third of life, paired difference above 0)
The entity that listens to boredom survives better than the one that can only walk in circles (deaths per 10k, paired difference below 0)
The entity that listens to boredom keeps the hidden need at least half full in the last third of life (median)
It finds depth: in at least 90% of worlds it masters skill level 3 or deeper
It finds depth sooner than the entity that ignores boredom (steps until level 3 is mastered, worlds where both get there, paired difference below 0)
ALL minus IGN = -89 [-368, -8.46] steps in 48 worlds
It is still worse than the informed reference (deaths per 10k, paired difference above 0): learning from boredom alone does not fully match knowing the ladder
It dies of the hidden need less often than the entity that ignores boredom (paired difference below 0)
The P263 result is not an artefact of tuning: with the learners' DEFAULT settings the hidden-level difference ALL - IGN is also above 0
